JOIN THE 2026 COMMUNITY CUP FROM AUG. 1-31 | LEARN MORE

TUESDAY
260825

2 rounds for total reps of:
On a 3-minute clock:
400-meter run
Max chest-to-bar pull-ups

Rest 1 minute

On a 3-minute clock:
400-meter run
Max handstand push-ups

Rest 1 minute

On a 3-minute clock:
400-meter run
Max dumbbell goblet squats

Rest 1 minute

♀ 35-lb dumbbell
♂ 50-lb dumbbell

Post total reps to comments.

Stimulus and Strategy:
Today, you'll take on an interval-style workout with a focus on higher-skill gymnastics at a fast pace. Push hard on each run to give yourself as much time as possible with each gymnastics movement. Plan to finish each run in under 2 minutes, so you have 1 minute or more for max reps of each gymnastics movement. The dumbbell loading should be light enough to hang on to it for the entire remaining time in the interval. Once you get through all 3 sets, start back at the beginning and move through each 3-minute AMRAP again.

Stimulus and Strategy:
Today's descending workout has weighted walking lunges and strict deficit handstand push-ups. The goal is to complete the workout in 10 to 15 minutes.

Choose a dumbbell load that requires minimal rest breaks; aim for at least 50-foot intervals with no more than about 10 seconds of rest when you break. Hold the dumbbell any way you choose, provided it supports quality movement.

The strict deficit handstand push-up will test raw upper-body inverted pressing. Expect to need several sets to complete each round. As a guide, if you can do sets of 3 for 20-15-10-5 reps with no more than 10 seconds of rest between sets, attempt this workout Rx'd. Today, we'll find the most challenging gymnastic scale for the handstand push-up before scaling to dumbbell overhead presses. Let sets and hard-capped rest times guide your chosen volume and movement variation.

I could have chalked up yet another 5km row but I had already spent a considerable amount of time going in and out of my sweltering garage today that even the thought of long duration monotonous movement in there was demotivating. Plus, I know that I can still row a 5km and keep it sub-20. So, what are my options: ride a 10km, run a 5km, or swim? I know that 500m is not a comparable time domain or amount of work (for me), and it has been a while since the last time I did a continuous swim distance longer than that. How about 1km, can I still do it continuous and in a similar time domain as a 5km row or run? The answer was no to the time, but I'm not really bothered by the time because I got an even longer duration bout of work than the row would have been and I proved to myself that I can still crank out 1km in the water without stopping (and no regular training time in the pool).
